tianjiApi.hint: Tianji OpenAI-compatible endpoint: exposes Tianji (tools / approvals / sessions included) as /v1/chat/completions for OpenClaw (WeChat ClawBot) or any OpenAI-compatible client. In OpenClaw set base_url to the address below, api_key to the key here, and model to tianji. Once WeChat ClawBot is bound to OpenClaw via QR, you can chat with Tianji inside WeChat.
tianjiApi.baseUrlHint: base_url: {{baseUrl}}　model: {{model}} (localhost only; use a tunnel for external access. In OpenClaw the Base URL ends at /v1 — do not append /chat/completions)

aiHub.title: AI Hub
aiHub.shortcutHint: e.g. Ctrl+Alt+K. Change if it conflicts.
aiHub.suggest: Predict the next prompt after every answer
aiHub.suggestHint: The prediction costs one extra model call (counted in the usage table below). Turning it off only removes the chip; Q&A is unchanged.
aiHub.bubbleHint: The panda girl in the corner: pat head / belly / skirt for play only, hold for a hug, double-click opens AI Hub, drag to snap; the right-click menu swaps the skin and opens settings. It mirrors the agent — trots while commands run, nudges you on approval, petals when a round lands; affinity grows as you pet it. Shortcut and tray still open the hub too.
aiHub.petImportEmpty: No custom art yet — import some to unlock this skin.
aiHub.petImportNeedIdle: Assign at least one frame to “Idle”, or the pet has nothing to play.
aiHub.petImportHint: Pick several images, or one n×n sheet: this machine keys out the background, trims each pose and normalises them onto one baseline — nothing leaves your computer.
aiHub.petLicenseHint: Only import art you may redistribute. Most eye-catching open-source pet packs are marked “no commercial use / attribution / share-alike” — keep them out of the installer.
aiHub.petSizeHint: Edge length of the pet window. Switching only affects that window; it re-snaps by its bottom edge and does not jump.
aiHub.petQuietHint: No speech bubbles and no confetti — moods show only through motion. It still knocks when a step waits for you.
aiHub.petResetHint: Affinity returns to 20 and the pet goes back to the bottom-right of the primary screen. Both only affect this pet.
aiHub.diffConfirm: Show the diff before the agent writes
aiHub.diffConfirmHint: At edit level, a file change asks you first (with the diff). Denying leaves the file untouched.
aiHub.rememberedEmpty: Nothing remembered yet — approve a step with「Always allow」and it lands here.
aiHub.webAllowHint: One per line or comma separated; subdomains are included (example.com also allows api.example.com). Empty under the allowlist tier = no fetch. https only, private hosts blocked, every fetch asks first.
aiHub.webTierHint: Off = no web tools. Allowlist = only listed hosts. Open = any public https (private hosts still blocked); every fetch still asks.
aiHub.webSearchHint: web_search is only offered when a provider and key are set. The key stays on this machine.
aiHub.mcpEmpty: None yet. One row is enough: a name (goes into tool names), a command, and its arguments.
aiHub.mcpAdded: Added {{name}}; it applies from the next question
aiHub.mcpHint: Each question starts every enabled server once to list its tools (npx cold start takes a second or two); tools are named mcp_fs_read_file, and each call starts a fresh process that is closed right after. A server decides what its tools can do, so below full access every call asks you first. A server that fails to start only costs this round a few tools; the question still works.
aiHub.subagentsHint: Lets the model hand a wide search to a read-only sub-agent: up to 16 rounds, only 800 characters of findings come back, so the main conversation does not fill with raw matches. It cannot edit files, ask you anything, or spawn another sub-agent. Costs more than a single search.
aiHub.subagentWrite: Let sub-agents edit files / run commands
aiHub.subagentWriteHint: Requires "Allow read-only sub-agents". When on, a sub-agent can also use write / edit / run_command / delete (to Recycle Bin) / move, but only at Edit permission or above (Read / Review never get it). Every write or command reuses the main turn's safety: conflicted repos are refused, protected paths are blocked, Edit shows an approval card first, and undo is shared with the main turn. It still cannot spawn another sub-agent.
aiHub.rememberedScope: Remembered at the narrowest known scope: with a repo selected it is stored per repo + current branch, so switching branch or repo asks once more; only a repo-less session stores it globally. With several service repos selected there is no single branch, so it is stored for the whole workspace.
aiHub.taskModeHint: Auto by default: no tool narrowing. Pin a scene temporarily with /mode in the composer; a dismissible chip shows above the input while pinned.
aiHub.profileHint: A profile only adds a tone/technical hint to the system prompt and may override temperature; what the AI may do is still decided by the permission level.
aiHub.harnessSources: Project: {{project}} · Global: {{global}} (`.ai-workbench/` holds context.md, memory.md, skills/*.md, hooks.json)
aiHub.harnessHint: Pick a repo first; without `.ai-workbench/` the global config in app data is used.
aiHub.planFirstHint: Enables a real plan gate: read-only exploration and update_plan first, then exit_plan_mode waits for your approval before write/command tools unlock. One-line questions are unaffected.
aiHub.parallelReadsHint: Read-only work (reading files, searching, listing folders, locating symbols) may run up to 4 at a time, which shortens the wait. Turn it off to run them strictly one by one: slower, but the steps appear in exactly the order the model asked for them.
aiHub.retriesHint: Automatically backs off and retries up to 3 times when the provider returns 429 (rate limit) or 5xx. Turn it off to fail immediately — useful when the provider bills duplicate requests or you want the real error right away.
aiHub.grepIgnoreHint: Search and find-files skip whatever .gitignore excludes (node_modules, build output). Turn it off to search those folders too — handy for generated code, slower and noisier.
aiHub.contextTokensHint: How many tokens each round may carry (48k by default). Past that it trims in three stages: tool results, then the oldest rounds, then the system prompt. Larger remembers more, but every request costs more and takes longer.
aiHub.resultCapHint: Upper bound for one tool result fed back to the model (12k characters by default); the head and tail are kept, with a hint on how to read on. Smaller saves tokens but cuts long logs and big files into smaller pieces.
aiHub.anthropicStreamHint: On by default: the answer appears word by word. Some relay gateways break SSE mid-stream; turn it off to send a plain request instead — the answer then shows up only once it is complete.
aiHub.mcpEnabledHint: Master switch. When off, this round starts no server processes and offers no mcp_* tools — the whole table below is paused; each server's own toggle still applies.
aiHub.freshContextHint: On by default: questions asked within two minutes reuse the last git snapshot, after a fingerprint check that nothing changed. Turn it off to re-collect every time — always the latest state, at the cost of a short wait per question.

usage.title: AI usage overview
usage.hint: Calls and estimated tokens from AI Hub / reports / commits — stored locally, never uploaded.
usage.todayOver: Today {{used}} / {{cap}} tokens — over budget ({{pct}}%, {{calls}} calls). This only warns; questions are not blocked.
usage.trendBudget: Dashed line = daily budget; bars over it turn red
usage.emptyTrend: No usage in the last 14 days.

data.title: Data
data.exportWarn: Export contains plaintext API keys / tokens. Do not share or upload.
data.importWarn: Import will overwrite all local data. This cannot be undone.

about.title: About
about.clearSkipHint: After clearing, v{{version}} will be offered again
about.skippedCleared: Un-skipped v{{version}} — it will be offered again on next start
about.privacyNote: API keys are stored in local SQLite only — do not share the database file

wecom.title: WeCom bot
wecom.hint: Connect via WeCom intelligent-bot long connection (Bot ID + Secret). Outbound only — no public callback URL. DM defaults to pairing; groups default to allowlist. WeCom usually only delivers group messages that @ the bot.
wecom.corpHint: Business APIs (docs / calendar / smartsheet) require a self-built app's Corp ID + Secret (WeCom admin → Application Management). The bot Bot ID/Secret is only for the message channel and cannot call business APIs.
wecom.corpHintShort: Only needed for docs / calendar / smartsheet; can be left blank.
wecom.engineHint: Tianji uses this app's models and four permission tiers; DeepSeek Harness hands the turn to the local DSH (a resident dsh --profile acp process) and keeps DSH's own model and sign-in. Switching reconnects the channel automatically; DMs and groups share the same engine.
wecom.engineHintShort: Tianji uses this app's models; DSH uses the local DSH models and sign-in. Switching reconnects.
wecom.dshPermNote: The DSH engine maps this tier onto its sandbox: Read-only → read-only; Edit / Review → workspace-write (DSH has no "AI reviews first", so both behave the same); Full → unrestricted and never asks. Approvals become approval codes in the chat. Tianji-only safety (conflict repos, protected paths, command blocklist, delete-to-recycle-bin) applies to the Tianji engine only.
wecom.dshPermHintShort: Maps onto DSH's sandbox and approval policy; approvals become chat codes.
wecom.dshWorkspaceHint: The DSH engine needs an absolute path (it is also the writable workspace); leave blank to use the current Git workspace.
wecom.dshMirrorNone: Not mirrored yet (syncs automatically once the channel is on)
wecom.dshMirrorHint: The managed acp profile mirrors DSH's web profile: bundle list, node_modules junction and the model-related patch layers. After changing plugins or models in DSH, hit "Re-sync".
wecom.dshMirrorHintShort: Mirrors DSH's web profile into acp; hit Re-sync after changing plugins.
wecom.dshResynced: DSH config re-synced, the engine is restarting
wecom.dshModelsHint: {{count}} models grouped by provider; models, keys and sign-in all come from DSH itself. "Auto" picks a model that has credentials each turn.
wecom.dshModelsEmpty: No usable model in DSH: configure a model and key on the Harness → Models page, then hit "Refresh models".
wecom.dshModelsOff: Turn the channel on (DSH engine) to load the model list automatically.
wecom.fullConfirm: Full permission can control this PC and may be triggered from WeCom. Continue?
wecom.requireMentionHint: WeCom usually only pushes group messages that @ the bot; this switch only changes welcome/hint copy. Add the group to the allowlist to use it.
wecom.requireMentionHintShort: Only affects welcome/hint copy; allowlist the group first.
